symbols.name: orthogonal residual
symbols.meaning: The orthogonal residual of an edge, the orthogonal complement of its smaller label inside its larger label.
symbols.quote: The orthogonal residual $\Delta$ of an edge is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one.

symbols.name: residual basis
symbols.meaning: An orthonormal basis of the residual $\Delta$, whose vectors give one two-point kernel each.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal{O}$ be an orthonormal basis of $\Delta$: a set of vectors $v$ with $v\cdot v=1$ and $v\cdot v'=0$ for distinct $v,v'\in\mathcal O$.

symbols.name: head label
symbols.meaning: The label at the head of an edge, whose frame is applied last along that edge.
symbols.quote: An edge runs from a tail label $U$ to a head label $V$, and its frame change is $C_VC_U^{-1}$.

symbols.name: kernel sign
symbols.meaning: The sign, plus or minus one, that decides whether the kernel for basis vector $v$ on this edge is forward or inverse.
symbols.quote: Let $\varepsilon_v\in\{1,-1\}$ with $\varepsilon_v\equiv\mathrm{wt}(v)\pmod 4$ on an increasing edge and $\varepsilon_v\equiv-\mathrm{wt}(v)\pmod 4$ on a decreasing edge.

symbols.name: two-point kernel
symbols.meaning: The operator $\tau_0 I+\tau_1 X_v$ for a binary vector $v$, a translation kernel.
symbols.quote: Since $X_v^2=I$, the operator $\Theta_v=\tau_0 I+\tau_1 X_v$ has inverse $\tau_1 I+\tau_0 X_v$, because $(\tau_0 I+\tau_1X_v)(\tau_1 I+\tau_0X_v)=2\tau_0\tau_1 I+(\tau_0^2+\tau_1^2)X_v=I$.

symbols.name: kernel coefficient
symbols.meaning: The complex number $(1+i)/2$, the coefficient of the identity in a two-point kernel.

symbols.name: kernel coefficient
symbols.meaning: The complex number $(1-i)/2$, the coefficient of the translation in a two-point kernel.

symbols.name: label projection
symbols.meaning: The projection onto a nondegenerate subspace $W$ along its orthogonal complement $W^\perp$.
symbols.quote: For a nondegenerate subspace $W$, $P_W$ is the projection onto $W$ along $W^\perp$.

symbols.name: diagonal operator
symbols.meaning: The operator on functions of addresses that multiplies the value at each address $x$ by a given function of $x$.
symbols.quote: For a function $f$ on addresses, $\mathrm{diag}_x(f(x))$ is the diagonal operator that multiplies the value at each address $x$ by $f(x)$.

symbols.name: integer representative
symbols.meaning: The integer, zero or one, that represents a binary value $b$.
symbols.quote: For $b\in\mathbb F_2$, $[b]\in\{0,1\}$ is its integer representative.

symbols.name: support
symbols.meaning: The set of coordinates at which a binary vector is one.
symbols.quote: For a binary vector $z$, $\mathrm{supp}(z)$ is the set of coordinates at which $z$ is $1$, and $\mathrm{wt}(z)=|\mathrm{supp}(z)|$ is its Hamming weight, read as an integer.

symbols.name: standard basis vector
symbols.meaning: The address with a single one at position $\delta$, one of the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb F_2^m$.
symbols.quote: For general $m$, take the route $U_0=\{0\}$ and $U_\delta=\mathrm{span}(e_1,\dots,e_\delta)$ for $1\le\delta\le m$, where $e_1,\dots,e_m$ is the standard basis and $e_\delta$ has a single $1$ at position $\delta$.

symbols.name: route step
symbols.meaning: The index of a step along the coordinate route, running from one to $m$.
symbols.quote: For general $m$, take the route $U_0=\{0\}$ and $U_\delta=\mathrm{span}(e_1,\dots,e_\delta)$ for $1\le\delta\le m$, where $e_1,\dots,e_m$ is the standard basis and $e_\delta$ has a single $1$ at position $\delta$.

relations.quote: The complex phase network is built on the [subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md).
The network takes its addresses from the [binary field](binary-field.md).
The complex phase network is indexed by [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md): each vertex carries one label $U$, a subspace with $U\cap U^\perp=0$.
The complex phase network computes its frames by the [tensor power](tensor-product.md) $H^{\otimes m}$ of $H$, where $\otimes$ is the Kronecker product.
The complex phase network has coefficients in [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md): each entry of $C_U$ and of $C_U^{-1}$ is a Gaussian integer divided by $2^m$.
